notes.val_seeds: Dataset v1's 24 validation seeds (finetune.json), re-rendered in dataset v2 (docs/eval/dataset-v2-freeze.json lists every one of them as a training seed), chosen before any v2 clip was rendered. The detector derivations (docs/eval/detector-plan.md, kit-colour-plan.md) already use these seeds as their validation clips. A validation seed whose clip fails the render checks is removed, not replaced (as seed 111 left v1's validation): ninety.vision.pod_clips writes the config the run uses and records the removal.
notes.stride: Every 5th frame (5 fps): nearer frames are near copies of each other.
notes.resolution: 640, divisible by patch 16 x windows 2. At the default 512 the median ball is 7.1 px (docs/eval/dataset-stats.json); 640 gives about 8.9 px for a 1.6x cost. Larger is a measured ablation, not a default.
notes.batch: 4 images, gradients accumulated 4 times: an effective batch of 16, rfdetr's default target. It was 2 x 8 (the same optimisation, half the memory) while training on a 24 GB Mac, where 4 x 4 took about 18 GB of unified memory; a 24 GB GPU holds 4 x 4.
notes.epochs: Up to 8 with early stopping (patience 3): the model already detects players and the ball after 30 epochs of v2/v2los; this adapts it to engine-v1 renders. Set before the run.
notes.seed: Fixed so a rerun on the same data gives the same model, up to GPU nondeterminism.
notes.num_workers: 8 data-loading workers on the GPU machine: with 2 the RTX 4090 sat at 13-23% busy while the loader ran at 90% CPU. Speed only; the data and the order of training are unchanged.
notes.purpose: The look-freeze fine-tune (docs/eval/finetune-v2freeze/PLAN.md): ours-freeze continues from ours-v4 (--init) on dataset v2's training clips only (280 seeds rendered at aea01f4 on one GPU pod, less the validation seeds and any clip that fails the render checks), so the demo's detector is trained in the look the demo shows. Every training setting equals finetune-round2.json; only val_seeds differ. Set before any v2 clip was rendered.
notes.lr: Half of finetune.json's (5e-5, encoder 7.5e-5), the usual choice when continuing from a trained checkpoint, so the adaptation does not undo what it learned. Set before the run.
notes.time_cap: 110 minutes of training on the pod (scripts/finetune-on-pod.sh), so the run, with export and copy-back, stays within the 2 hours the Coordinator set. A run stopped at the cap keeps its best validation checkpoint so far, and its manifest says it was stopped (train.py --record-only). Expected 60 to 95 minutes: ours-v2 took about 9 minutes an epoch on a 4090 for 12,650 images; this run has about 12,800.
